title: Local separatedness under base change and composition
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], using their sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. An immersion of algebraic spaces means a representable morphism all of whose scheme base changes are immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is locally separated if its diagonal $X\to X\times_YX$ is an immersion. If $f$ is locally separated, then for every morphism $Y^{\prime}\to Y$ the projection $X\times_YY^{\prime}\to Y^{\prime}$ is locally separated. If $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ are locally separated, then $g\circ f$ is locally separated. Every morphism of schemes, regarded as a morphism of algebraic spaces, is locally separated.

proof.text: First note directly from the scheme-test definition that immersions of algebraic spaces compose. For immersions $A\to B\to C$ and a scheme test $h_T\to C$, the sheaf $h_T\times_CB$ is represented by a scheme $W$ with $W\to T$ an immersion. Testing $A\to B$ on $h_W\to B$ gives a scheme $V=h_W\times_BA$ with $V\to W$ an immersion. On each test scheme the projection $(t,b,a)\mapsto(t,a)$, with inverse $(t,a)\mapsto(t,\operatorname{image}(a),a)$, identifies $h_V$ with $h_T\times_CA$. By clause (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], $V\to W\to T$ is an immersion. This proves both representability and the required immersion condition for the composite.

source.place: spaces.tex Tag 02YV (lemma-composition-immersions), expanded scheme-test proof; schemes.tex Tag 02V0 (lemma-composition-immersion).

proof.text: For base change put $X'=X\times_YY'$, $P=X\times_YX$, and $P'=X'\times_{Y'}X'$. These are algebraic spaces by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The map $q:P'\to P$ forgets the $Y'$-coordinate. On every test scheme a section of $P'\times_PX$ consists of $((x_1,y'),(x_2,y'),x)$ with $x_1=x=x_2$ and $f(x)=\operatorname{image}(y')$. Sending it to $(x,y')$ gives a natural bijection with $X'$, inverse $(x,y')\mapsto((x,y'),(x,y'),x)$. Its projection to $P'$ is exactly $\Delta_{X'/Y'}$. Thus this diagonal is the base change of $\Delta_f$ along $q$. Since $\Delta_f$ is an immersion, its base change is an immersion by [lem-sfb-space-immersion-affine-tests], proving local separatedness of $X'\to Y'$.

For composition put $P=X\times_YX$ and $Q=X\times_ZX$. The map $r:Q\to Y\times_ZY$ sends $(x_1,x_2)$ to $(f(x_1),f(x_2))$. The pullback of $\Delta_g:Y\to Y\times_ZY$ along $r$ has sections $(x_1,x_2,y)$ satisfying $f(x_1)=y=f(x_2)$. Forgetting $y$ is a natural bijection with $P$, inverse $(x_1,x_2)\mapsto(x_1,x_2,f(x_1))$. Hence $j:P\to Q$ is a base change of $\Delta_g$, and is an immersion by [lem-sfb-space-immersion-affine-tests]. All products exist as algebraic spaces by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The composite $j\circ\Delta_f$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$, so equals $\Delta_{g\circ f}$. Both factors are immersions by the two local-separatedness hypotheses; the scheme-test argument of step 1 makes their composite an immersion. This proves the composition assertion.

proof.text: Finally let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. By the universal property in [def-pc-fibre-product], maps $T\to X\times_YX$ are exactly compatible pairs of maps $T\to X$; therefore $h_{X\times_YX}=h_X\times_{h_Y}h_X$, compatibly with diagonals. The scheme diagonal is an immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-diagonal-immersion]. For every scheme test $h_T\to h_{X\times_YX}$, Yoneda [lem-pc-yoneda] identifies the test with a scheme map $T\to X\times_YX$; its pullback is the scheme fibre product, and its projection to $T$ is an immersion by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft]. Thus the diagonal of $h_f$ is representable with every scheme base change an immersion, exactly the required local separatedness.
